title: Quick check: Testing in Continuous Integration

questions.prompt: In the context of “Testing in Continuous Integration” and “Running tests automatically”, What should a unit test focus on?
options: A small unit of logic with controlled inputs and clear expected results.
Whether a button matches a screenshot only.
questions.answer_key: A small unit of logic with controlled inputs and clear expected results.
questions.explanation: Unit tests target small units; integration and end-to-end tests are needed for broader boundaries and user journeys.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Testing in Continuous Integration”, Which tests are especially useful for important user journeys?
options: Only unit-testing strings and assuming the whole application works.
End-to-end tests that exercise routing and interactions in a browser-like environment.
Running no tests when a route is changed.
questions.answer_key: End-to-end tests that exercise routing and interactions in a browser-like environment.
questions.explanation: End-to-end tests help verify behavior across routes, server boundaries, and client interactions.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Testing in Continuous Integration”, What should a meaningful regression test do?
options: Reproduce the previously failing case and assert the behavior that should remain fixed.
Repeat a vague manual click without an expected result.
Delete the failing test after the fix.
Check only that the code compiles even when runtime behavior was wrong.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the previously failing case and assert the behavior that should remain fixed.
questions.explanation: A stable regression test captures the failure mode and expected behavior so later changes do not silently reintroduce it.

review_note: Draft question set with module-specific concepts. Review item wording and answer accuracy before publication; learner-facing APIs should expose prompt/options only and release correctness feedback after grading.
